summary: Full-page PDF reader with selectable text, selection translate/ask, and a floating 'pet' assistant. pdf.js is vendored (Apache-2.0, pinned) because the browser's built-in PDF plugin exposes no selection to JS. New endpoints POST /api/qa, POST /api/translate and GET /api/qa?key=, a qa_history table, and reader/assistant UI replacing the small inline preview.
scope_note: Covers the diff since commit fd149a5, including the vendored pdf.js build (~1.7 MB). One real paper_qa and one real selection_translate call.

budget_impact.rationale: Two new runtime model paths (paper_qa, selection_translate) were exercised. Both were already registered operations, so no ceiling or price changed; calls are ledgered in .local/app/usage.jsonl and degrade with a visible message when refused.
budget_impact.before: paper_qa and selection_translate were registered but unused at runtime.
budget_impact.after: Both are wired through the gateway; observed spend $0.000166 (397 tokens) and $0.000030 (53 tokens).

additional_checks.scope: pdf.js served; real answers; history persisted; ledger recorded both operations

reviews.reviewer: Implementing agent; feature work, not recommendation quality

open_risks: Selection depends on our text layer; the native fallback cannot select.
Only the abstract plus the selection is sent; answers are bounded by it.
Reader renders eagerly; large PDFs are not optimised.
Vendored pdf.js must be updated deliberately (pinned 4.6.82).
Recommendation quality remains unproven; gates stay not_run.
